# Jubilees Chapter 17 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 17:4 — "bond-woman" vs. "slave woman"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "bond-woman" | Archaic KJV rendering |
| LOGOS | "slave woman" | Modern standard |
| PNEUMA | "slave woman" | Same as LOGOS |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS/PNEUMA "slave woman." "Bond-woman" is archaic; "slave woman" accurately renders Ge'ez amhat. All three agree on the meaning; only register differs.

---

## 17:10 — "cast him under a tree" vs. "placed him"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "cast him under a tree" | Literal — the Ge'ez verb suggests throwing/casting |
| LOGOS | "placed him under a tree" | Gentler verb |
| PNEUMA | "laid him under the tree" | Same as LOGOS, slightly different verb |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. The Ge'ez verb here is ambiguous between "lay down" and "cast/throw." In context of a desperate mother with a dying child, "placed" is slightly more natural than "cast" while preserving the emotional intensity.

---

## 17:16 — "there were voices in heaven"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "there were voices in heaven regarding Abraham" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "there were voices in heaven concerning Abraham" | Same, slight word change |
| PNEUMA | "voices broke out in heaven about Abraham" | "Broke out" adds drama |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Voices in heaven" is the Ge'ez rendering — a divine assembly scene. PNEUMA's "broke out" is vivid but adds urgency not implied in the source. "Concerning" vs. "regarding" — minor; LOGOS preferred.

---

## 17:17 — Mastema's request: "bid him" vs. "command him"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "bid him offer him as a burnt-offering on the altar" | "Bid" |
| LOGOS | "Command him to offer Isaac as a burnt offering on the altar" | "Command" |
| PNEUMA | "Tell him to offer Isaac as a burnt offering on the altar" | "Tell" |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Command" accurately renders the Ge'ez imperative; Mastema is requesting that God issue a divine command to Abraham. "Bid" (EMET) is archaic; "tell" (PNEUMA) is too informal for a divine command.

---

## 17:19 — "his soul was not impatient" vs. "never grew impatient"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "his soul was not impatient, and he was not slow to act" | Literal double negative |
| LOGOS | "his soul was not impatient and he was not slow to act" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "He never grew impatient. He never dragged his feet" | Converted to vivid active positives |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. The double-negative formulation ("not impatient, not slow") is a Ge'ez rhetorical pattern worth preserving. PNEUMA's conversion to "never grew impatient / never dragged his feet" is readable but loses the parallel structure.

---

**Total disagreements: 5**
